title: If you could take credit for any movie ever created, which movie would it be?

commenti.body:
Assuming I get a cut of the box office, Star Wars.

Words for the bot, Words for the bot, Words for the bot, Words for the bot, Words for the bot, Words for the bot, Words for the bot,

Since this ain't exactly ethical... Probably some Aaron Sorkin movies. Hesitating between Steve Jobs and The Social Network, but I'll probably pick The Social Network since it was made by David Fincher and starred the likes of Jesse Eisenberg, Andrew Garfield and Justin Timberlake. Hah! If only it was me getting credited for all that amazing and impeccable and perfectly sounding dialogue...

Aware I don't deserve it but wth. Scarface, Apocalypse Now, Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas, Goodfellas, Taxi Driver, Pulp Fiction, Snowpiercer, Kung Fu Hustle, Fallen Angels, Chungking Express, In the Mood For Love, Rebels of the Neon God, Harakiri, The Thing(1982), then home alone.

The Truman Show

Words for the bot, Words for the bot, Words for the bot, Words for the bot, Words for the bot, Words for the bot, Words for the bot, Words for the bot,
and in case I don’t see ya, good afternoon, good evening, and words for the bot.

Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind. 


I believe Charlie Kaufman is a genius.



Words for the bot, words for the bot, blah, blah, blah. Words for the bot, words for the bot, blah, blah, blah. Words for the bot, words for the bot, blah, blah, blah. Words for the bot, words for the bot, blah, blah, blah.

I would love to say I've written a bunch of Hitchcock movies. I'd also like to say I could write a screwball comedy. I just find that writing style so intricate and detailed and impressive. 

Words for the bot 
Words for the bot 
Words for the bot 
Words for the bot 
Words for the bot

Harold and Maude or Life Is Beautiful. They both explore the full spectrum of the human experience. With both films, it took multiple viewings to comprehend all the layers. I like that in a movie. I get hit with the raw emotion during the first viewing and then go back in to absorb the nuances. In my opinion, they have both stood the test of time. I’m not sure how they did at the box office, but in terms of wanting credit for creating something amazing, they have my vote.
Good pics! I’d add anything (in addition to Home Alone) done by John Hughes!

chungking express, pulp fiction, aftersun or past lives. i had 0 expectations from past lives so i got really really surprised with how good it was. the direction and cinematography is both beautiful and clever

I would 100% want to be credited with writing and directing There Will Be Blood - I saw it opening weekend and after it ended, I turned to my wife and said “that was the greatest movie ever made.”

I’ve been a PTA fan for years but there’s something about TWBB that really struck me on a primal level. I felt it was made especially for me. I’ve probably watched it over 100 times at this point (6 in the theater) and it just gets better and better with subsequent viewings. I absolutely love it.
